results.question: How often can I do an IRA-to-IRA rollover?
results.answer: You can make only one rollover from an IRA to another (or the same) IRA in any 1-year period, regardless of how many IRAs you own. The rule applies by aggregating your IRAs, and the 1-year period begins on the date you receive the IRA distribution. Trustee-to-trustee transfers are not limited. These excerpts also say this limit does not apply to rollovers from traditional IRAs to Roth IRAs (conversions).

The excerpts also say that under the 10-year rule, beneficiaries who are not taking life expectancy payments must withdraw the entire balance by that date.
